records.title: AQME chemistry automation
question_patterns: what does AQME do in EasyROB
do i need to generate descriptors

user_guidance.purpose: AQME generates descriptors from structures such as SMILES. It is optional for a model-ready descriptor CSV. For descriptor files only, press Run AQME; for an integrated model from SMILES, stay on ROBERT, check Enable AQME Workflow, and press Run ROBERT.
when_to_use: AQME is needed when the CSV contains structures such as SMILES but lacks relevant molecular descriptors. It is not needed when useful descriptor columns are already present.
prerequisites: For AQME generation, provide a main CSV with valid SMILES. For supervised model training, also select the target, prediction type, and ROBERT workflow.
steps: Choose standalone descriptor output or the integrated model workflow according to your goal.
user_guidance.result: The selected run control produces standalone descriptor tables or generates and uses descriptors in the ROBERT model workflow.
next_steps: Opening the AQME tab is not required for ordinary molecular descriptors; use it for advanced settings or atomic descriptors with common-substructure selection.
common_issues: A CSV containing only SMILES has structures but not model-ready descriptors; a valid descriptor CSV can be used directly without AQME.

records.title: When AQME is not needed
question_patterns: do I need AQME if my CSV already has descriptors

user_guidance.purpose: Clarify that descriptor generation is conditional rather than a mandatory step in every EasyROB run.
when_to_use: Skip AQME when the main CSV already contains valid descriptor columns compatible with the intended ROBERT workflow.
prerequisites: Confirm that the descriptor table is complete, numerical where expected, and includes the target for model training.
steps: Leave Enable AQME Workflow unchecked, load the descriptor CSV, and configure ROBERT directly.
user_guidance.result: ROBERT uses the supplied descriptors without recalculating them from structures.
next_steps: Select the target, prediction type, and ROBERT workflow.
common_issues: A CSV that contains only SMILES is a structure table, not a ready descriptor table.

records.title: Generate descriptors and train a ROBERT model
question_patterns: how do AQME descriptors reach ROBERT
how do I go from SMILES to a ROBERT model
how can i generate descriptors before i run the model
how do i generate descriptors to train a model

user_guidance.purpose: Generate molecular descriptors automatically from SMILES and use them immediately to train the selected ROBERT model.
when_to_use: Use this integrated path when the goal is a ROBERT model and the main CSV contains valid SMILES rather than ready descriptor columns.
prerequisites: Load the main CSV with valid SMILES and complete the normal ROBERT target, prediction type, and workflow settings.
user_guidance.result: QDESCP generates a descriptor CSV, which EasyROB loads into the configured ROBERT workflow before continuing with model training automatically.
next_steps: Open the AQME tab only for advanced options such as common-pattern atom selection for atomic descriptors; it is not required for ordinary molecular descriptor generation.
common_issues: Do not use Run AQME when the intended result is an immediate model run; Run AQME is the separate descriptor-only action.

user_guidance.purpose: Calculate molecular and, when valid mapped atoms are selected, atom-specific descriptors from chemical structures.
when_to_use: QDESCP is the AQME module most directly relevant to EasyROB descriptor generation.
prerequisites: Valid structures and any required atom mapping; solvent and descriptor-level choices should match the intended calculation.
steps: For ordinary molecular descriptors, use Enable AQME Workflow from the ROBERT tab. Open the AQME tab only when atomic or atom-specific descriptors, common-substructure atom selection, or advanced AQME options are needed.
user_guidance.result: QDESCP writes denovo, interpret, and full descriptor datasets for inspection or ROBERT input.
next_steps: Choose the descriptor table that balances interpretability and coverage for the next analysis.
common_issues: Atom-specific settings require valid mapped atoms across the relevant molecules.

user_guidance.purpose: Explore plausible molecular conformations before later geometry or quantum-chemistry stages when conformer sampling is needed.
when_to_use: Use CSEARCH in a broader AQME workflow that explicitly requires conformer exploration.
prerequisites: A suitable molecular structure and a reason to sample conformations beyond direct descriptor generation.
steps: Configure CSEARCH in an AQME workflow outside the basic EasyROB descriptor path.
user_guidance.result: CSEARCH provides conformer candidates for downstream processing such as CMIN or QPREP.
next_steps: Continue with the required upstream chemistry stages before QDESCP.
common_issues: CSEARCH is not automatically required for every EasyROB QDESCP workflow.

records.title: CMIN module
question_patterns: is CMIN part of descriptor generation

user_guidance.purpose: Minimize or refine conformer geometries before later calculations when the selected chemistry workflow requires that preparation.
when_to_use: Use CMIN after conformer generation when geometry refinement is part of the intended AQME protocol.
prerequisites: Conformer structures and an appropriate minimization setup.
steps: Run CMIN on selected conformers before preparing downstream quantum calculations.
user_guidance.result: CMIN produces refined structures for later AQME stages.
next_steps: Continue to QPREP, QCORR, or QDESCP as required by the chosen protocol.
common_issues: CMIN is an upstream option, not an automatic requirement for every EasyROB descriptor run.

user_guidance.purpose: Prepare input files for supported quantum-chemistry calculations when those calculations are part of the AQME workflow.
when_to_use: Use QPREP after suitable structures exist and a quantum calculation must be launched.
prerequisites: Prepared geometries plus the intended quantum method, basis, charge, multiplicity, and execution environment.
steps: Configure the quantum calculation and create its input files with QPREP.
user_guidance.result: QPREP produces calculation inputs for external quantum-chemistry execution.
next_steps: Run the calculation, then use QCORR to inspect and organize its output when applicable.
common_issues: QPREP is not automatically required for a direct EasyROB descriptor workflow.

user_guidance.purpose: Inspect quantum-chemistry outputs, organize successful calculations, and identify failures that may need corrected inputs.
when_to_use: Use QCORR when descriptor generation depends on completed quantum calculations whose outputs need validation.
prerequisites: Quantum output files produced from an appropriate calculation workflow.
steps: Run QCORR on the output set and review detected problems before reusing results.
user_guidance.result: QCORR separates usable results from calculations that require attention or resubmission.
next_steps: Correct failed calculations or continue with QDESCP using validated results.
common_issues: QCORR is not automatically required for every EasyROB descriptor workflow.

user_guidance.purpose: Supply molecular structures in a SMILES column that AQME can validate, compare, map, and convert into descriptors.
when_to_use: Use SMILES input when the main CSV does not already contain the needed molecular descriptors.
prerequisites: Each relevant row needs a valid SMILES string; train and optional test data must support the same mapping contract when atom descriptors are used.
steps: Load the CSV through Select Input CSV File on ROBERT, then enable the AQME tab to inspect the common pattern.
user_guidance.result: AQME receives the structures from the main CSV; there is no separate AQME file selector.
next_steps: Choose descriptor options and inspect atom mapping before running AQME.
common_issues: Missing or invalid SMILES prevents structure-based descriptor generation.

records.title: Descriptor Level
question_patterns: which descriptor level should I choose
what are interpret denovo and full

user_guidance.purpose: Choose which QDESCP descriptor table is passed to ROBERT when AQME is integrated into Run ROBERT: interpret, denovo, or full.
when_to_use: Review the level when descriptor count and interpretability matter for an integrated Run ROBERT workflow.
prerequisites: Valid structure input and a clear plan for how the descriptor table will be used.
steps: For integrated Run ROBERT, select Descriptor Level before starting. Standalone Run AQME does not use Descriptor Level and generates denovo, interpret, and full tables.
user_guidance.result: Integrated Run ROBERT uses the chosen descriptor table, while standalone Run AQME always produces all three tables for comparison.
next_steps: Inspect the generated columns before selecting a table for ROBERT.
common_issues: More descriptors are not automatically better for a small modelling dataset, and changing this selector does not limit standalone Run AQME output.

records.title: Solvent
question_patterns: what does the solvent option change

user_guidance.purpose: Control whether a supported solvent setting is passed to QDESCP for descriptors that depend on the calculation environment.
when_to_use: Change solvent only when the scientific protocol calls for an available solvent treatment.
prerequisites: Confirm that the intended AQME method supports the solvent choice.
steps: Review the Solvent selector; the current interface offers None, which sends no solvent keyword.
user_guidance.result: A supported non-None choice would alter applicable calculations, while None leaves solvent-specific settings unset.
next_steps: Continue with descriptor and atom settings.
common_issues: Do not claim a solvent was modelled when the selector remained None.

records.title: Atom selection and mapping
question_patterns: how do I select atoms for descriptors

user_guidance.purpose: Select atoms in the common molecular pattern so QDESCP can calculate consistent atom-specific descriptors.
when_to_use: Use atom selection only when atomic descriptors are scientifically useful and the shared pattern maps unambiguously.
prerequisites: Valid SMILES, a displayed common SMARTS pattern, and consistent mapped atoms across train and optional test molecules.
steps: Click atoms in the molecule viewer and inspect the highlighted, numbered mapping before running.
user_guidance.result: Selected atoms are stored in the mapped SMILES contract used for atomic descriptor ordering.
next_steps: Resolve ambiguity or metal warnings, then run AQME.
common_issues: Never guess an atom when several pattern matches are possible.

records.title: Multiple SMARTS matches
question_patterns: why are there multiple atom matches
which highlighted atoms should I choose

user_guidance.purpose: Warn that the common pattern matches a molecule in more than one way, so atom positions may not be uniquely defined.
when_to_use: Review this diagnostic before requesting atomic descriptors from an ambiguous pattern.
prerequisites: The molecule viewer must show the detected pattern and highlighted candidate atoms.
steps: Inspect the highlighted or mapped structure, compare it with the intended chemistry, and select only the intended atoms.
user_guidance.result: A deliberate mapping avoids assigning atom descriptors to inconsistent positions.
next_steps: Run AQME only after the mapping represents the same chemical role across molecules.
common_issues: If ambiguity cannot be resolved confidently, omit atomic descriptors rather than guessing.

records.title: Detected metal atoms
question_patterns: what happens when AQME detects a metal

user_guidance.purpose: Show when metal atoms were detected and may be highlighted or selected for atomic descriptor generation.
when_to_use: Review the metal diagnostic for organometallic or coordination structures before accepting automatic atom choices.
prerequisites: Valid structures and a molecule viewer state that clearly identifies the detected metal.
steps: Inspect the highlighted structure and confirm that the intended metal and surrounding mapping are chemically correct.
user_guidance.result: Confirmed metal mapping lets QDESCP target the intended atom consistently.
next_steps: Resolve any simultaneous multiple-match warning, then run AQME.
common_issues: Do not assume the first highlighted match is correct when several metals or pattern matches exist.

records.title: AQME descriptor CSV files
question_patterns: which descriptor CSV goes to ROBERT

user_guidance.purpose: Provide tabular molecular descriptors generated by QDESCP for inspection, independent analysis, or ROBERT modelling.
when_to_use: Use an output table after AQME finishes and before starting a descriptor-based ROBERT workflow.
prerequisites: A successful descriptor run and, for supervised modelling, a target column associated with the molecules.
steps: Choose the denovo, interpret, or full CSV appropriate to the task and load it through Select Input CSV File.
user_guidance.result: The descriptor CSV becomes the ROBERT main table rather than passing raw structures directly to model training.
next_steps: Select the ROBERT target and prediction type, then run the modelling workflow.
common_issues: If the generated table lacks a target, add the correct measured values before supervised model building.
